# Match

Header: `winui/ui/hosting/ContentHost.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/spec/Dynamic.hpp`.

A node that owns exactly one child and can replace it at runtime. [Layout](item-layouts.md#uilayout), rendering, input, focus and animation all pass through to the child, so wrapping a subtree in one changes nothing visible about it.

It has two uses. The first is a swappable slot for UI whose structure varies (a wizard page, a master/detail pane): [`ui::Match`](#uimatch) builds one and rebuilds its child when a [Property](../core/property.md) changes. The second is a base class for a control made of one child plus its own chrome (a card, a padded group). Unlike most controls it is not `final`: override [measure_override()](#measure_override), [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) and [render_override()](#render_override), and call the [ContentHost](#uicontenthost) version for the child. [Border](../layout/border.md#uiborder) and [DensityScope](../layout/density-scope.md#uidensityscope) derive from it.

Example: 
```cpp
// A reusable card: padding plus a rounded background, the child forwarded.
class Card final : public ui::ContentHost
{
public:
    explicit Card(std::unique_ptr<ui::Element> child)
    {
        set_child(std::move(child));
    }

protected:
    ui::Size measure_override(ui::Size available, const ui::MeasureContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Size inner = ui::ContentHost::measure_override(
            ui::Size{std::max(0.0f, available.width - 32.0f), std::max(0.0f, available.height - 32.0f)},
            context);
        return ui::Size{inner.width + 32.0f, inner.height + 32.0f};
    }
    void arrange_override(const ui::Rect& final_rect, const ui::ArrangeContext& context) override
    {
        ui::ContentHost::arrange_override(final_rect.inset(ui::Thickness{16.0f}), context);
    }
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Theme& theme = context.theme;
        renderer.fill_rounded_rect(bounds(), 8.0f, theme.colors().background);
        ui::ContentHost::render_override(renderer, context); // then the child
    }
};

// As a runtime-swappable slot:
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::ContentHost* slot = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ContentHost>());
slot->set_child(std::make_unique<Card>(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Step 1")));
ui::ButtonControl* next = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Next"));
next->on_click([slot] { slot->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Step 2")); });
window.set_content(std::move(stack));
```

## `ui::Match`

Structure driven by a value: one node showing the subtree that belongs to the current value. Builds a [ui::ContentHost](#uicontenthost).

[`.value`](#uimatch-value) is what to look at, usually `ui::bind(prop)`, and [`.content`](#uimatch-content) turns it into the subtree to show. The subtree is built once at construction and again on every change of the value. The [Property](../core/property.md)'s equality gate drops writes that change nothing, so a redundant assignment costs nothing. Only this node's subtree is rebuilt, so the cost grows with the subtree, not with the screen.

By default a change destroys the old subtree, so what the user typed or scrolled in it is gone and handles published from inside it through [`.control`](#uimatch-control) dangle afterwards. That is right for pages whose state should reset. [`.keep = true`](#uimatch-keep) keeps every subtree it has built and only hides the ones not current, so tab pages and master/detail panes come back as they were left.

Name the value's type, `ui::Match<Page>{.value = page, ...}`: C++ deduces a spec's type only from the field's own type, which a [Property](../core/property.md) is not.

LIFETIME: [`.content`](#uimatch-content) is stored on the built node and invoked for the life of the tree, so it must not capture anything shorter-lived than the window. Capturing a reference to model state the caller owns is the intended shape. A bound [Property](../core/property.md) that dies first stops the rebuilds.

Example: 
```cpp
enum class Page { Home, Settings };
ui::Property<Page> page{Page::Home};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::HorizontalStack{.spacing = 8, .content = {
        ui::Button{.text = "Home",     .on_click = [&] { page = Page::Home; }},
        ui::Button{.text = "Settings", .on_click = [&] { page = Page::Settings; }},
    }},
    ui::Match<Page>{
        .value   = page,
        .keep    = true, // the check box is still ticked after a visit to Home
        .content = [](const Page& p) -> ui::Spec
        {
            switch (p)
            {
            case Page::Home:     return ui::Text{.text = "Welcome home"};
            case Page::Settings: return ui::CheckBox{.text = "Dark mode"};
            }
            return {};
        },
    },
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Match{
    .value, .keep, .content_transitions, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width,
    .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible,
    .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus,
    .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uimatch-value"></span>`value` | `ui::Binding<T>` |  | The value to match on: a plain value (built once) or `ui::bind(prop)`, which shows the content for the new value whenever the property changes. |
| <span id="uimatch-keep"></span>`keep` | `bool` | `false` | false: a change destroys the old subtree and builds the new one. true: each value's subtree is built the first time the value is seen and kept until the [Match](#uimatch) goes, hidden while another one shows, so it keeps its state. One subtree is kept per distinct value, which suits a handful of pages; for a value with no bound on how many there are, use a [ui::ForEach](for-each.md#uiforeach) or a view instead. |
| <span id="uimatch-content_transitions"></span>`content_transitions` | `ui::Binding<ui::TransitionList>` |  | Transitions for a change of content: with a [ui::ContentTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-contenttransition) the new subtree slides and fades in while the old one fades out. Not used with [`keep`](#uimatch-keep). |
| <span id="uimatch-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uimatch-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uimatch-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uimatch-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uimatch-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uimatch-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uimatch-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<std::type_identity_t<ui::Match>>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. Named through std::type_identity_t so that passing a handle does not take part in deducing the type argument. |
| <span id="uimatch-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Callback<ui::Spec(const std::type_identity_t<T>&)>` |  | Produces the subtree for a given value. Its parameter names T through std::type_identity_t so that [`.value`](#uimatch-value) alone decides T when the type argument is left out. |

## `ui::Lazy`

A subtree that is built the first time it is shown. Builds a [ui::ContentHost](#uicontenthost).

[`.visible`](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec) on any spec hides a subtree that already exists. [Lazy](#uilazy) is the same thing for a subtree that is expensive to build and that most users never open: [`.content`](#uilazy-content) is a function, and it runs the first time [`.visible`](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec) is true. After that the subtree is hidden and shown again without being rebuilt, so it keeps its state. While hidden the [Lazy](#uilazy) takes no room.

[`.unload = true`](#uilazy-unload) destroys the subtree whenever [`.visible`](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec) turns false and builds it again on the next true: the memory is given back, and the state is lost.

LIFETIME: [`.content`](#uilazy-content) is stored on the built node, so it must not capture anything shorter-lived than the window.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Spec log_view()
{
    return ui::Text{.text = "Started."};
}

ui::Property<bool> show_log{false};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::ToggleSwitch{.header = "Show the log", .checked = show_log},
    ui::Lazy{
        .visible = show_log,
        .content = []() -> ui::Spec { return log_view(); }, // not built until switched on
    },
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Lazy{
    .visible, .unload, .content_transitions, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width,
    .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment,
    .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus,
    .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

| <span id="uilazy-content_transitions"></span>`content_transitions` | `ui::Binding<ui::TransitionList>` |  | Transitions for the content: with a [ui::ContentTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-contenttransition) it slides and fades in when it is built and, with [`unload`](#uilazy-unload), fades out when it goes. |
| <span id="uilazy-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uilazy-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uilazy-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uilazy-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uilazy-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |

## `ui::State`

[State](#uistate) that belongs to a piece of UI instead of to the app. Builds a [ui::ContentHost](#uicontenthost) that owns an `S` and shows what [`.content`](#uistate-content) makes of it.

A component that needs a private flag, a text being edited or a small struct of Properties has nowhere to keep it: a local variable is gone when the function returns, and the handlers that captured it dangle. [State](#uistate) gives it a home in the tree. The node constructs one `S`, passes it to [`.content`](#uistate-content) by reference, once, and destroys it after the subtree. So a handler or a binding inside the subtree may capture that reference: it lives exactly as long as they do.

[`.content`](#uistate-content) runs once. It is not run again when the state changes; what changes on screen is what was bound to the state. `S` is usually a [ui::Property](../core/property.md) or a struct of them. [State](#uistate) shared between components still lives in the caller and is passed in as [`Property<T>&`](../core/property.md).

[`.initial`](#uistate-initial) returns the starting state. It is a function because a [Property](../core/property.md) cannot be moved; left out, the state is `S{}`.

Example: 
```cpp
// A disclosure row whose "open" flag belongs to the row, not to the app.
ui::Spec disclosure(std::string title, ui::Callback<ui::Spec()> body)
{
    return ui::State<ui::Property<bool>>{
        .content = [title = std::move(title), body = std::move(body)](ui::Property<bool>& open) mutable -> ui::Spec
        {
            return ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
                ui::Button{.text = std::move(title), .on_click = [&open] { open.toggle(); }},
                ui::Lazy{.visible = open, .content = std::move(body)},
            }};
        },
    };
}
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::State{
    .initial, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uistate-initial"></span>`initial` | `ui::Callback<S()>` |  | Makes the starting state, constructed in place in the node; `S{}` when left out. |
| <span id="uistate-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uistate-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uistate-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uistate-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uistate-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uistate-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uistate-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::State>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uistate-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Callback<ui::Spec(S&)>` |  | Builds the subtree from the state, once. The reference stays valid for as long as the subtree lives, so handlers and bindings inside may capture it. |

## `ui::ContentHost`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

A node that owns exactly one child and can replace it at runtime. [Layout](item-layouts.md#uilayout), rendering, input, focus and animation all pass through to the child, so wrapping a subtree in one changes nothing visible about it.

It has two uses. The first is a swappable slot for UI whose structure varies (a wizard page, a master/detail pane): [`ui::Match`](#uimatch) builds one and rebuilds its child when a [Property](../core/property.md) changes. The second is a base class for a control made of one child plus its own chrome (a card, a padded group). Unlike most controls it is not `final`: override [measure_override()](#measure_override), [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) and [render_override()](#render_override), and call the [ContentHost](#uicontenthost) version for the child. [Border](../layout/border.md#uiborder) and [DensityScope](../layout/density-scope.md#uidensityscope) derive from it.

Example: 
```cpp
// A reusable card: padding plus a rounded background, the child forwarded.
class Card final : public ui::ContentHost
{
public:
    explicit Card(std::unique_ptr<ui::Element> child)
    {
        set_child(std::move(child));
    }

protected:
    ui::Size measure_override(ui::Size available, const ui::MeasureContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Size inner = ui::ContentHost::measure_override(
            ui::Size{std::max(0.0f, available.width - 32.0f), std::max(0.0f, available.height - 32.0f)},
            context);
        return ui::Size{inner.width + 32.0f, inner.height + 32.0f};
    }
    void arrange_override(const ui::Rect& final_rect, const ui::ArrangeContext& context) override
    {
        ui::ContentHost::arrange_override(final_rect.inset(ui::Thickness{16.0f}), context);
    }
    void render_override(ui::Renderer& renderer, const ui::RenderContext& context) const override
    {
        const ui::Theme& theme = context.theme;
        renderer.fill_rounded_rect(bounds(), 8.0f, theme.colors().background);
        ui::ContentHost::render_override(renderer, context); // then the child
    }
};

// As a runtime-swappable slot:
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::ContentHost* slot = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ContentHost>());
slot->set_child(std::make_unique<Card>(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Step 1")));
ui::ButtonControl* next = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ButtonControl>("Next"));
next->on_click([slot] { slot->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("Step 2")); });
window.set_content(std::move(stack));
```

### ContentHost

```cpp
ContentHost() = default
```

An empty host; it measures to nothing until [set_child()](#set_child).

### set_child

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_child(std::unique_ptr<T> child)
```

Takes ownership of the child and returns a non-owning observer, the same convention as [StackControl::add()](../layout/stack.md#add). Replaces and destroys the previous child, then updates the layout and redraws. A null [`child`](#child) leaves the host empty, like [clear_child()](#clear_child).

With a [ContentTransition](../tree/element-transitions.md#struct-contenttransition) among the [children_transitions()](../tree/element.md#children_transitions) the change is animated: the new child slides and fades in while the old one fades out over it. The old child is out of layout, input and the tab ring at once, and destroyed when its exit has played.

Safe to call from a handler of the child being replaced: while a [Window](../tree/window.md) is dispatching, the old child is destroyed only once that dispatch has returned.

### clear_child

```cpp
void clear_child()
```

Destroys the current child, leaving the host empty (it then measures to nothing). Updates the layout and redraws.

### orphan_child

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> orphan_child()
```

Takes the child out alive and hands it back, leaving the host empty, for adding it somewhere else. Focus inside it is cleared and it plays no exit transition. Null when the host is empty. Updates the layout and redraws.

### child

```cpp
Element* child() const
```

The current child as a non-owning observer, or nullptr when empty.

### hit_test_transparent

```cpp
bool hit_test_transparent() const override
```

True while the host has no child, or its child is not Visible: the pointer then reaches what is behind the host. A host that draws something of its own (a background, a header) overrides this to return false.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

Lists the child, if any.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

The child's desired size, or zero when empty. A subclass adding chrome calls this with the space left over, then adds its own.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Gives the child the whole of `final_rect`; a subclass passes the inset rect instead.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Renders the child; a subclass draws its chrome first, then calls this.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the exit animation of a replaced child.
